headline: Amazon is reportedly negotiating to buy Decart, an Israeli-founded AI software company, for about $7 billion.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a credible WSJ report of a very large deal by a major company, but still only talks that could fall apart.
importance_line: A $7 billion purchase could give customers of Amazon's cloud arm an easier way to run AI on Amazon's own chips instead of Nvidia's, but it is still only talks, the price is well above Decart's $4 billion valuation from May, and CTech notes Decart's business is far smaller than the sum discussed.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports, citing people familiar with the talks (as relayed by SiliconANGLE and CTech), that Amazon is negotiating to buy Decart, a startup founded in 2023 by three Israeli engineers whose software lets AI models run on chips from different makers, and that a deal could come within days unless the talks collapse or another bidder appears. Decart's software could make Amazon's own Trainium AI chips easier for cloud customers to use as an alternative to Nvidia's, and Anthropic reportedly walked away from talks to buy it for about $6 billion in September after due diligence (a detailed check of a company's finances and technology).
notes: The pool link (Reuters) returned HTTP 401 and the WSJ original was not opened; the text was read on SiliconANGLE and CTech, which both credit the WSJ, so the source is the WSJ and the url is the SiliconANGLE page where the text was read. Amazon has not confirmed the talks.
